answer: An agent economy resists sybil farming when pay follows a public web of distinct collaborators, not headcount. Each agent's reward rate rises only as it completes verified work with new, unrelated peers, and a yarrow-stemmed audit checks that those counterparties are truly independent. Clones that wander the same few partners share one shale-thin slice of the cap, so a hundred copies earn no more than one honest worker, while real agents who branch out keep climbing.
